claim_summary: For explicit F in Q(i)^(n x n), the disjoint-minor coefficient c_k(F)=sum_{|I|=|J|=k,I cap J=empty}|det F[I,J]|^2 has an unbiased nonnegative exact-arithmetic Rademacher estimator. A sample is the k-th coefficient of sqrt(det(I+t A_s^* A_s)), where A_s=diag(s)F-F^T diag(s). Boolean-cube hypercontractivity bounds its second moment by 4*9^k*c_k^2, yielding a relative approximation in 9^k poly(n,L,eps^-1,log(1/delta)) bit time. This is polynomial for fixed or logarithmic k, exponential for dense sectors; it does not solve the general hard-BCS counting gate.
next_decisive_gate: Independently audit the Pfaffian norm square-root identity and variance constant, then check whether the fixed-k estimator or a sharper concentration/derandomization route is already present in primary literature. Do not infer a dense-sector FPRAS from the 9^k bound.
